newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's Coptic Pope says Arabs lost Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's Coptic Pope says Arabs lost Jerusalem.

text.p: The leader of Egypt's six million Christian Copts was quoted on Saturday as saying Arabs had lost Jerusalem to Israel because of their lack of unity.

"(Israeli Prime Minister) Netanyahu is exploiting Arab weakness...If they present a united and strong front, he will back down," Pope Shenouda III told the London-based Arabic daily Al-Hayat in an interview.
"Jerusalem was all in the hands of the Arabs, then it was divided...and as the days passed the Arabs lost it completely and the number of Jews increased," he added.
The fate of Jerusalem, holy to Christians, Moslems and Jews, is one of the thorniest issues in Middle East peace talks.

Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and later annexed it, declaring the whole city its enternal capital. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of their future state.
Israel and the PLO agreed in a 1993 interim peace deal to leave negotiations on Jerusalem to "final status" talks which must be completed by 1999.
"I now fear that Israel will wipe out any remaining Arab existence in Jerusalem," Shenouda said.
Netanyahu has irked Arabs since he was elected in May by increasing Jewish settlement activity around Jerusalem.

Shenouda is a staunch critic of Israel and has banned Copts from going there since 1970 when Israel took over the Coptic monastery of Deir al Sultan in Jerusalem and handed it over to Ethiopian monks.
Last year Shenouda refused to give communion to thousands of Copts who defied his ban on visiting Jerusalem last Easter despite a 17-year-old peace treaty between Egypt and Israel.
